History restore and Apply Order to Query each replace the editor through one undoable action.

Messages render errors and info messages with different foreground colours, including the expected light-theme error red.

Failed query results select the Messages tab, while successful results and editor diagnostics leave the selected Results tab unchanged.
Result-column auto-size enablement and width round-trip through QSettings; save-time widths clamp to 50–2000, while stored out-of-range values and booleans restore the 300 px default.

Preferences persist result-column auto-size enablement and maximum width, apply them to the active view, and restore the 150 px policy in a fresh MainWindow.

History deletion removes matching stable ids while preserving record order, supports multiple ids, ignores unknown ids without a write, skips empty deletion requests without a write, and preserves the migrated id of a legacy survivor.
Review 11 adds independent guards that an unknown id does not call _write_history and that deleting a known v2 id migrates a raw v1 survivor on disk.

History SQL export serialises valid records newest-first into exact comment-prefixed SQL blocks, preserves embedded comments and trailing spaces, normalises terminal line endings to one blank separator and one final newline, and skips missing or non-string queries.

History SQL export compares actual instants across mixed UTC offsets, treats naive timestamps as UTC without comparing naive and aware datetime instances directly, and retains unparseable timestamp records after all parseable records.
History delete confirms the selected record count, removes multiple selected records only after confirmation, and refreshes the visible rows.
Cancelling a history deletion preserves every selected record and every visible row.
History supports Ctrl multi-selection; a context click within it preserves the selection, while a context click on another row selects only that row.
Selected history records save as one atomically written SQL file through MainWindow, appending .sql to an extensionless destination.
Cancelling the history SQL save dialog creates no file.

The shared history-SQL destination normaliser appends .sql only when no suffix was supplied, while direct Qt dialog-wrapper tests cover suffix-less, .sql, explicit alternate suffix, and cancellation paths.

Catalog cell selection keeps a single clicked File cell selected, while Copy Alias and Remove operate on that cell's current row; an actual QTest vertical-header click selects every cell in the corresponding row.

Schema Type-cell selection keeps exactly that cell selected while retaining its row's column name, preserves a two-row cell selection when its context menu opens, and lets a QTest vertical-header click select the whole row.

design_decisions: A QScintilla keyPressEvent override compares the incoming QKeySequence to one module-level Ctrl+/ sequence, triggers the existing Toggle Comment QAction, accepts the event, and delegates every other event to the base class.
The QScintilla stub requires a non-optional QKeyEvent and parameter name e; the implementation matches that contract while retaining a defensive None return.
PyQt's QTest stubs model the static helpers as instance methods, so the focused test keeps the required runtime calls and uses narrow no-matching-overload suppressions.
The existing QAction retains WidgetShortcut context for its menu presentation; the key event route is what makes the shortcut work in QScintilla.
Undoable editor replacements use QScintilla's selection API inside one beginUndoAction/endUndoAction pair, then reset scroll-width tracking exactly as the destructive setText override does.

Toggle Comment preserves its existing per-line prefix and indentation logic, replaces the transformed document through QScintilla's selection API in one undo action, restores the edited line range when text was selected, and restores the prior cursor position when it was not.

Selection restoration uses the visible text length after stripping CR/LF from QScintilla's line text, because lineLength includes EOL characters and would otherwise normalise a non-final-line selection onto the following line.

Replace All now delegates its unchanged replacement-count calculation to the existing set_text_undoable helper, preserving the no-match early return while grouping the replacement as one native QScintilla undo action.

MessagesPanel resolves severity colours from its own palette's Base role, keeping theme detection local to the widget and avoiding a settings dependency. Light uses error #b3261e, warning #7a4e00, info #005ac1; dark uses #ffb4ab, #ffb95d, and #a8c7fa.
MainWindow owns the results QTabWidget so only failed query results can select its existing MessagesPanel; successful query results and editor diagnostics retain the caller's current tab.

Auto-size preferences use versioned results keys and the preview-limit quartet shape: the enablement value requires a real bool, while width is save-clamped to 50–2000 and restores the 300 px default for invalid persisted values, including bool.

ResultTableView owns an enabled/max-width auto-size policy with defaults True/300, samples at most 200 rows for content sizing, auto-sizes after every populated frame only when enabled, and caps only visible columns so manual Auto-size Columns uses the same cap.

PreferencesDialog exposes the existing auto-size settings as a checked-by-default checkbox and a 50–2000 px spin box. Accepting it persists the policy and applies it through ResultTableView.set_auto_size_policy; MainWindow restores the same policy after creating the result view.

HistoryManager.delete_records materialises requested ids before loading history so an empty request returns without writing; non-empty requests filter the migration-aware get_all result, retain source order, and atomically rewrite only when an existing record was removed.

Review 11's mixed raw v1/v2 fixture deletes the known v2 id without an earlier get_all call, so it proves delete_records itself migrates an on-disk legacy survivor. A mocked unknown-id deletion independently proves the conditional write guard.

The pure history exporter sorts parseable persisted timestamps by actual instant descending, normalises naive timestamps to UTC for a safe mixed comparison, places unparseable timestamps afterward while preserving their caller order, preserves every timestamp verbatim in its comment line, and uses rstrip on only CR/LF terminal characters so SQL trailing spaces remain intact.

HistoryDock keeps one reusable Delete QAction, enables it from the current stable-id selection when the context menu opens, and builds a transient menu around that action. A context click outside the existing selection resets to that item; one inside it preserves the multi-selection. Confirmed deletion delegates to HistoryManager.delete_records before refresh. Round-15 review established that Qt's mouse press already produces both selection outcomes, so the explicit block remains as intent and keyboard-menu coverage rather than a test-proven branch.

HistoryDock owns a reusable Save as SQL action but only emits selected full records; MainWindow owns the save dialog and uses write_atomically with the pure serializer. The dialog adapter normalises only extensionless destinations to .sql, preserving a user-supplied suffix.

Review 16 extracts history-SQL suffix handling into normalise_sql_destination so both production and fake adapters share one caller-visible rule; direct Qt wrapper tests prove its suffix-less, explicit-suffix, and cancellation behaviour.

CatalogDock uses SelectItems plus ExtendedSelection, but every context action resolves its target from selectionModel().currentIndex() rather than selectedRows(), so a single selected cell continues to identify its owning entry.

SchemaPanel uses SelectItems with its existing ExtendedSelection. Its context menu preserves a clicked selected cell's multi-cell selection, while an unselected context-menu target becomes the sole current selected cell.
